summary: Full backend + frontend test of the 'Meine Weltreise' streaming extension. 17/17 pytest cases pass (auth, content, admin RBAC, uploads, episodes/seasons/countries CRUD, security roundtrip, brute-force lockout). Playwright covers viewer login, search, country filter, episode modal, admin login, all 8 admin tabs, and logout — all pass. Credentials restored to original values after roundtrip tests.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout key is IP-based, but the backend sits behind a reverse proxy that shows multiple upstream client IPs (10.219.0.x). Lockout can be evaded by hitting different pods and also affects legitimate users sharing the same NAT. Consider hashing X-Forwarded-For + a global sliding window per credential, or fetching real client IP.

Once locked, EVERY subsequent request (including correct credentials) returns 429 for 15 min — a legitimate user can't recover. Consider verifying credentials first and only enforcing lockout after wrong ones (or shorter cooldown).
Deleting a season does NOT cascade to its episodes; orphan episodes remain (dev comment acknowledges this).

action_items: Consider treating check_bruteforce more carefully: verify credential first, only enforce lockout on wrong attempts, and use the real client IP (X-Forwarded-For) to avoid multi-pod evasion & shared-NAT false positives.
Optionally cascade-delete episodes when a season is deleted, or reject season deletion while episodes exist.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py verify_pw runs bcrypt on strings that come straight from JSON — fine, but consider a max length cap to avoid CPU DoS (bcrypt is O(n)).
/api/admin/upload streams file content to disk before finishing size check — the current implementation is correct (streams in 1 MB chunks and aborts if over MAX_UPLOAD_MB).

Cookies are Secure+SameSite=lax + httpOnly — good; but no CSRF token on state-changing endpoints. Since SameSite=lax + JSON body + no simple GET mutations, risk is low but worth noting for future hardening.

seed_defaults uses INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD='changeme' default if env var missing — .env currently sets the correct value; if the env is ever removed/reset, admin will silently be seeded to 'changeme'. Consider failing fast when the initial password env var is missing.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL is loaded from /app/frontend/.env (conftest handles this). All login attempts appear from the reverse-proxy IP as far as the backend is concerned; if a test session leaves login_attempts entries behind, the conftest session fixture clears them at start & end. If running only a subset of tests you may need to clear /app/backend db.login_attempts manually. Brute-force test loops up to 20 wrong attempts because the ingress load-balances across pods so counts are split. Frontend uses raw HTML + data-testid attributes throughout.
